code_change_check.detail: The compiled symbol body differs from the pre-review object in compiler-generated C++ exception/landing-pad frame-state literals (0x106/0x102 and 0x7d97/0xaf5f) and in one stack-temporary register choice. The retail-visible .tex/.lmp load order and the two early-return paths were re-checked against the current source; no behavioural change is claimed from the object diff alone, so fresh evidence was generated.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja recovers one function 0x004C5F00-0x004C6156 (599 bytes, 20 blocks, 30 edges); radare2 recovers the same 20/30 node and edge sets; angr CFGFast recovers the exact entry with no unresolved jumps. The candidate entry is igi::retail::terrain::Terrain_LoadTexturesAndLightmaps at 0x00460910 (335 bytes, 12 blocks, 16 edges) in igi1.exe 35d92a3a, delegating the file work to TerrainLevelData::Terrain_LoadLightmaps at 0x0045f5f0 (4896 bytes, 182 blocks, 268 edges).

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Retail is x86 cdecl: context at [esp+4], path/name pointer at [esp+8] (Binary Ninja prototype int32_t(void* arg1, int32_t arg2)). The candidate takes void* context and const char* base_path in the same order and word count. Retail copies the string and appends '.tex' then '.lmp'; the candidate derives a terrain directory with base_path.parent_path() and reads TERRAIN.LMP, a documented host adaptation.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: Retail builds the palette as 256 dwords of i<<16, stores the texture package at context+0xDBC, the palette at +0xDF4, and the lightmap table/count at +0xDF8/+0xE00, with a 0x2C page stride. The host bridge uses typed ModelTexture/lightmap containers and a 256-entry palette; no literal constant equivalence is claimed.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail's byte-addressed context offsets (+0xDBC, +0xDF4, +0xDF8, +0xE00) and 0x484-byte stack frame are deliberately replaced by TerrainLevelData members in the host bridge. There is no byte-identical memory layout to compare; the check cannot apply to this adapted implementation.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Retail calls Terrain_LoadTexturePackage (0x005175A0), Texture_UploadPalettePacket, Resource_FileExists, Resource_Load, per-page Texture_UploadMipmapPacket and Resource_Unload. The host bridge reads TERRAIN.LMP with std::ifstream and does not register the resource or upload retail packets; those side effects are intentionally not reproduced, so call/side-effect equivalence is out of scope.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail has one ret at 0x004C6156. It returns 0 at 0x004C600B when App_ContextGetTerrainLightmapsUsed()==0 and at 0x004C6096 when Resource_FileExists('<path>.lmp')==0; on the loaded path EAX is Resource_Unload's result (live retail observation 0x0000000A, the post-unload pool count). The candidate returns 0 on a null context or when the lightmap stage yields nothing, and does not register the .lmp, so it returns 0 rather than the pool count. The divergence is recorded and is why the record is not VERIFIED.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: Neither the retail body nor the candidate performs floating-point arithmetic. Binary Ninja's 'float arg2' typing for the second argument is a pointer typing artifact; the palette entries are integer i<<16.

limitations: Host-bridge scope: retail .tex texture-list load, 256-entry palette upload, per-page mipmap upload and Resource_Unload teardown are not reproduced; the candidate returns 0 instead of the retail pool-count result.
Retail context offsets and the 0x484-byte frame are host-adapted into typed TerrainLevelData members; no byte-identical layout is claimed.
Status is STRUCTURALLY_VERIFIED: retail structure and return paths were checked; CFG similarity 1.0 is Binary Ninja vs Radare2 agreement on the retail image, not candidate equivalence.
